An operator stands at one press for a whole shift, a tablet in hand. Not the plant, not the line: this one machine.
Through the shift they ask the same few things. What is it doing, and what is next for it?
What did I make, what did I put in, is it good, and is anything owed to the machine? One screen answers all of them.
Four words. A station is one machine's screen, made for the person standing at it, not for the office.
The queue is the work released to this machine, in the order it should run. Only released work is in it.
To book is to write down how many good and how many scrap, always against an order and its step.
To issue is to write down which lot of material went into that order, so it can be traced later.
The station screen of the fork mould, FORK1_Mold. The machine is chosen at the top; the operator starts the shift here.
First card, its state: running, and since when. Going down asks why, which is the next class.
Second card, its queue: the order it is running, WO-FORK1-0001, step 10, Mold, and how many good of how many ordered.
That count moves by itself: the mould's own counter books every shot it makes.
Third card, book output. Against: the order at the head of the queue, step 10. The operator counts a box.
Five hundred good, three scrap. Book.
Booked, against WO-FORK1-0001 step 10, under the name of the person signed in. The queue's count is up by five hundred.
Fourth card, issue material. It issues to the order running here, WO-FORK1-0001.
The lot is the fork line's polypropylene resin, LOT-PP-FORK1-001. Two kilos: about what five hundred forks weigh. Issue.
Issued. The lot is two kilos lighter, and the order now says which resin went into it.
Fifth card, quality, on what this machine is running: forks, UT-FORK. Only characteristics with a specification are offered.
Length: the specification is 164 to 166 millimetres. The operator puts a fork on the gauge.
165.1 millimetres: in spec. It is in the recent results, with the time and who measured it.
Last card, maintenance on this machine. Here, nothing is owed: this plant has no maintenance plan set up.
Where a plan is set up, the jobs due on this machine are listed here, and the operator can start and complete them.
Now what it refuses. This is the next fork order, WO-FORK1-0002. Its first step is on the same mould, but it is only planned.
Back at the mould, the Against list holds one order: WO-FORK1-0001. The planned order is not there to book against.
Nor is any order of another line. An operator can only book to work released to this machine.
And what it does not refuse. Type five thousand good: more forks than this mould has made since the plant started.
Booked. The station took the figure as typed. Nothing on the screen says the counter disagrees.
The queue now says the mould has made thousands more than its counter saw. A typed booking is added to the count; it is not checked against it.
So a typed figure is the operator's word. The audit trail says who typed it, and the counter's own shots stay counted beside it.
That is the station screen: one machine, read top to bottom, and the work done at it written down. You now know how to do three things.
